input.question: Why are there so many different kinds of cheese made from cow's milk, but cheese made from goat's milk is just "goat cheese".
input.ground_truth: It isn't just "goat cheese", it's just that your average American doesn't have enough experiences with goat cheeses to name any particular one. Feta, Kunik, Castelo Branco, and Clochette are all (at least partially) goat cheese that I've eaten personally. I'd think that pretty much everyone in the US has some experience with feta at a minimum.

Question: Why are there so many different kinds of cheese made from cow's milk, but cheese made from goat's milk is just "goat cheese".

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big box of Legos that are all the same color. You can build *lots* of different things with them—a house, a car, a spaceship! That’s like cow’s milk. People have made *many* different kinds of cheese from cow’s milk because cow’s milk is very common and comes in different types. People have been playing with it for a long, long time and found many ways to make it taste and look different.

Now, imagine you have a small box of Legos that are a different color—let’s say, brown. You can build things with them too, but most people just call them “brown Legos” because there aren’t as many of them and they mostly look and feel the same. That’s like goat’s milk cheese. There are fewer kinds of cheese made from goat’s milk, and most people just call it “goat cheese” because it usually tastes and looks pretty much the same every time.

So, there are many kinds of cow cheese because people have tried lots of ways to make it special. But goat cheese is usually just called “goat cheese” because it doesn’t change as much and people are used to it being one kind!
